entities.evidence: שֵׁם names Shem, who joins his brother Japheth in covering their father Noah.
וָיֶפֶת names Japheth alongside Shem. Both are sons of Noah, whom they cover with the garment.

וָיֶפֶת names Japheth alongside Shem. Both are sons of Noah, whom they cover with the garment.

analysis.evidence: אֶת־הַשִּׂמְלָה identifies the garment as the direct object. Shem and Japheth then put it on their shoulders, confirming that they first took it in hand.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ marks a Qal wayyiqtol. The verb is third-person masculine singular and precedes the compound subject שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת, agreeing with its first member.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת names Shem and Japheth as the pair who take the garment. שְׁנֵיהֶם (“both of them”) refers back to the pair, and אֲבִיהֶם (“their father”) identifies the man they cover as their father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Shem, son of Noah and brother of Japheth.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת names Shem and Japheth together. שְׁנֵיהֶם (“the two of them”) refers to the brothers who carry the garment and cover their father.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וָ means “and” and joins the personal name יֶפֶת to שֵׁם.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקַּח שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת אֶת הַשִּׂמְלָה, אֶת marks הַשִּׂמְלָה (“the garment”) as the definite direct object of וַיִּקַּח (“took”). Shem and Japheth took the garment.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the feminine noun שִׂמְלָה with the sense “garment.” The source gloss “despise” does not fit the object the brothers take and carry.
draft.definition: A garment that can be wrapped around someone as a covering.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 9:23 Shem and Japheth carry the garment across their shoulders and cover their father with it.

analysis.evidence: After וַיִּקַּח, the object marker אֶת introduces הַשִּׂמְלָה as the thing Shem and Japheth took. They laid it across their shoulders and used it to cover their father’s nakedness.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial שׂ of the feminine singular common noun שִׂמְלָה. The noun is in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: A garment used as a covering.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth take הַשִּׂמְלָה, “the garment,” which supplies the understood object of וַיָּשִׂימוּ. The phrase עַל שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם specifies where they laid it, across their shoulders.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural. The subject is Shem and Japheth.
analysis.sense: place something at a specified location

analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth place the garment עַל שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם, “on the shoulders of the two of them,” then walk backward to cover their father. The phrase identifies where each brother carries the garment.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state before שְׁנֵיהֶם, “the two of them.” The singular refers to one shoulder of each brother.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66311:2, 66073:1.
analysis.morphology: Masculine dual cardinal numeral in the construct state with a third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth put the garment on their shoulders and walked to cover their father. The following adverb אֲחֹרַנִּית specifies that they walked backward.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with Shem and Japheth as its subject.
analysis.sense: go, move from place to place

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּלְכוּ אֲחֹרַנִּית means “they walked backward.” Shem and Japheth approached their father with their faces turned away so they could cover him without seeing his nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew adverb of direction modifying וַיֵּלְכוּ.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth carry הַשִּׂמְלָה, the garment, on their shoulders and walk backward. The direct object אֵת עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם identifies what they covered as their father’s nakedness.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural. The subject is Shem and Japheth.
analysis.sense: to cover someone’s nakedness with a garment

analysis.evidence: אֵת introduces עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם, “their father’s nakedness,” as the direct object of וַיְכַסּוּ, “they covered.” The possessive suffix on אֲבִיהֶם makes the construct phrase definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth use the garment to cover עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם (“their father’s nakedness”). The verse repeats the phrase when it says that they did not see their father’s nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state, with אֲבִיהֶם (“their father”) as its possessor.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth cover עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם, “the nakedness of their father.” The suffix הֶם refers to the two sons, and אָב identifies their father, Noah.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲחֹרַנִּית describes which way their faces pointed as they covered their father. With their faces turned backward, they did not see his nakedness.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” פְנֵי is the plural construct form of פָּנִים, a noun of common gender. The third-person masculine plural suffix הֶם means “their” and refers to Shem and Japheth.

analysis.evidence: In וּפְנֵיהֶם אֲחֹרַנִּית, the adverb gives the direction their faces were turned. They faced away from their father as they covered him, so they did not see his nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb of direction with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked phrase repeats עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם, “their father’s nakedness,” as the object of לֹא רָאוּ, “they did not see.” It names what Shem and Japheth covered with the garment while facing away.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ is prefixed to עֶרְוַת, the feminine singular construct form of the common noun עֶרְוָה. The following אֲבִיהֶם supplies the possessor.

analysis.evidence: In וְעֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם לֹא רָאוּ, Shem and Japheth did not see their father’s nakedness. אֲבִיהֶם identifies their father, Noah, as the one whose nakedness they covered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix referring to Shem and Japheth.

analysis.evidence: לֹא immediately precedes רָאוּ (“they saw”). The clause states that Shem and Japheth did not see their father’s nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth faced backward as they covered their father. עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם is the object of רָאוּ, and לֹא negates the verb: they did not see their father’s nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with Shem and Japheth as the subject.
